14.t: Working with data: what forms, and how fast?
q: Explain the purpose of the flask with no sparks.
It is a control: it shows that the energy from sparks is needed, and that the amino acids are not contamination.
Compare the results with methane and ammonia with those with CO₂ and nitrogen.
The methane mixture gave far more: 18 against 1 mg glycine and 12 against 3 kinds of amino acid.
Most scientists now think the early atmosphere was mainly CO₂ and nitrogen. Evaluate the spark experiment as evidence for how amino acids first formed.

It shows amino acids can form without life. But the original gases were probably wrong, and CO₂ and nitrogen alone give little. With buffering the yield rises again (12 mg), so the idea is still plausible; other sources (vents, meteorites) are possible too.
Doubling the run time from 7 to 14 days barely raised the yield. Suggest why.
The reactant gases are used up, and sparks also break down some of the products.
Suggest why glycine and alanine form in the largest amounts.
They are the simplest, smallest amino acids, needing the fewest atoms and steps.

23.t: Working with data: dating the earliest life
q: Calculate how long after Earth formed LUCA lived.
4.54 − 4.2 = 0.34 billion years (about 340 million years).
Explain why LUCA is estimated to be older than the oldest accepted fossils.
Early cells were tiny and soft, so they rarely fossilised, and most rocks that old have been destroyed or changed by heat and pressure.
Outline how a molecular clock estimates the age of LUCA.
Count the differences in sequences of conserved genes between lineages; using a mutation rate calibrated with fossils, divide the differences by the rate to get the time since they split.
Evaluate the claim that life began within a few hundred million years of Earth forming.

Supported by liquid water at 4.4 and LUCA at about 4.2 billion years. But the clock assumes a steady mutation rate, the oldest fossils are disputed, and bombardment may have sterilised the surface. The evidence points to an early start, but it is not certain.
Suggest why the oldest possible microfossils are disputed.
Similar shapes can form from minerals without life, and the rocks have been heated and altered, so the structures are hard to interpret.
